headline: Jensen Huang to college grads: "Run. Don't walk" toward AI
liCaption:
Jensen Huang's commencement message to Carnegie Mellon graduates deserves your attention: "Run. Don't walk" toward AI. This isn't hype—it's a reality check from one of tech's most influential leaders about where opportunity truly lies in 2026.

Why this matters now is critical context. We're at an inflection point where AI has moved from experimental to essential across virtually every industry. Companies are actively recruiting talent with AI expertise, and the skills gap is widening rapidly. Huang's message reflects what we're seeing across the industry: the race for AI talent is accelerating, and waiting on the sidelines is no longer a viable career strategy.

From a business perspective, this has profound implications. Organizations that attract and develop AI-capable teams will gain significant competitive advantages. For emerging talent, entering the AI space now means joining projects that will literally shape the next decade of technology. The value creation potential is enormous, and early movers understand this viscerally.

The broader AI industry is in a growth phase that rivals the early internet boom, but with higher stakes and faster timelines. Unlike previous tech cycles, AI touches every sector—healthcare, finance, manufacturing, creative industries. This creates unprecedented opportunities across domain expertise, not just traditional tech roles.

Looking ahead, we'll likely see an even sharper divide between AI-fluent professionals and those still building traditional skill sets. The students taking Huang's advice seriously today will be the architects, leaders, and entrepreneurs commanding these emerging opportunities by 2030. The competitive advantage goes to those who commit now, not later.

The takeaway: In an AI-driven future, your career trajectory depends on how quickly you decide to engage with this transformation.

Source: Axios · https://www.axios.com/2026/05/11/jensen-huang-carnegie-mellon-commencement-ai
